official.description_text:
Researcher in ML and 6G KPI Prediction
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
Future networked systems increasingly integrate sensing, communication, and computation across large numbers of connected devices. Applications such as industrial automation, cyber-physical systems, and defence-related infrastructure require distributed AI systems that can operate reliably despite limited resources, uncertain communication, and potential adversarial conditions. Our research group studies various analytical and system-level aspects of such systems, with particular emphasis on edge computing, AI, and emerging 6G networks. The work in our group is always conducted in a collaborative environment within the division as well as with external academic groups and industrial partners.
One focus of the group is related to KPI prediction for mission-critical and low latency apliccations. Different KPIs such as coverage, throughput and latency typically evolve due to stochastic effects, however, data-driven prediction methods are becoming more and more relevant for future 6G communication networks. In this context we are seeking for a researcher candidate with experience in this field, that can advance our agenda further for instance through causal AI, extreme-value theory methods or temporal ML architectures and inference methods. The position involves collaborations within our research group as well as with other research groups from different disciplines and universities. It will also comprise collaborations with industrial partners
Qualifications
Requirements
A recent doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree
Research expertise in relevant topics
Strong publication record
Collaboration abilities, as well as independence
An understanding of mathematical tools required for the role, for instance, KPI prediction methods, machine learning and/or extreme value theory
Preferred qualifications
A track record with analytical or experimental research on related topics mentioned in the job description
Knowledge of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system in order to apply for this position. You are responsible to ensure that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Max two pages long.
Your complete application must be received by KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

The employment is valid for a limited time according to the agreement - for up to 6 months, with access according to agreement.

ai.summary: Fixed-term researcher position (up to 6 months) at KTH in machine-learning and 6G network KPI prediction, focusing on data-driven methods for predicting communication network performance metrics (coverage, throughput, latency) using causal AI, extreme-value theory, or temporal ML architectures. Requires recent PhD and strong publication record.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic overlap. The position is purely technical ML/telecommunications research (6G networks, KPI prediction, causal inference, extreme-value theory). The researcher's domain is human-centred XR, immersive learning, and spatial cognition. Communication-network optimization and edge-computing systems are entirely orthogonal to HCI, user experience, collaboration, or learning outcomes.

methodological_fit.rationale: No meaningful methodological fit. The position requires expertise in machine-learning algorithms, causal inference, temporal architectures, and extreme-value theory—pure ML/systems research with minimal overlap to the researcher's HCI and experimental-design background. Quantitative research and statistics skills are present but insufficient; the researcher lacks ML algorithm development, advanced statistical modelling, or systems-level optimization experience. This is excluded-direction territory (pure ML algorithm development).

growth_value.rationale: Growth value is minimal and contradicts stated research direction. Developing expertise in KPI prediction, causal AI, and 6G systems does not advance capabilities in human-centred immersive systems, spatial cognition, user evaluation, or collaborative learning. This represents movement into pure ML and systems engineering, the opposite of the researcher's target identity.

strategic_value.rationale: Limited strategic value. Although KTH is a strong institution, this role does not support the researcher's stated career direction (doctoral studies in human-centred XR, target institutions Aalto and TU Delft). A 6-month position in ML/6G networks would not strengthen candidacy for HCI-focused doctoral roles and could confuse research identity. The role prioritizes ML systems over human-centred research.

eligibility_flags: Researcher holds MSc by Research (not yet completed doctoral degree), so does not meet the stated requirement of a 'recent doctoral degree.'
Position explicitly requires strong publication record in ML/6G—researcher has one first-author journal article in XR/learning, insufficient track record in ML research.
No demonstrated expertise in required domains: KPI prediction, causal inference, extreme-value theory, machine-learning systems, or 6G networks.
risks: Researcher is ineligible: MSc by Research is not a doctoral degree.
Position is in an excluded direction (pure ML algorithm development) according to target-identity constraints.
Substantial competency gap: researcher lacks ML expertise, causal-inference methods, and extreme-value theory.
Six-month contract is very short for meaningful contribution to advanced ML research.
Position would reinforce technical/engineering identity rather than human-centred research identity, potentially complicating future doctoral applications to HCI groups.
